question: During the issuance of the new European-standard Greek identity card by the Hellenic Police to a citizen of the Republic of Cyprus residing in Greece since before 1974, it was discovered that the field for ‘place of birth’, which refers to a location currently situated in the occupied area of Cyprus, displays the name imposed by Türkiye instead of the correct, internationally recognised and official place name, based on the legitimacy of the Republic of Cyprus.

According to the competent Greek service, the incorrect indication comes from the European computerised system/digital platform used for issuing identity cards, in which the illegal Turkish names of places in Cyprus under Turkish occupation have apparently been registered, resulting in the adoption of the occupying authorities’ terminology.
This practice is unacceptable as it is contrary to international law and the European acquis. Can the Commission say: 1.

Is the Commission aware of the fact that the specific European information system/digital platform used by the Member States to issue official documents contains geographical references at odds with the official and internationally recognised nomenclature of the Republic of Cyprus?

Does it intend to take measures to ensure that place names on this European platform are corrected and to restore the officially recognised place names, as have been defined by the competent national authority, the Cypriot Permanent Committee for the Standardisation of Geographical Names of the Republic of Cyprus?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.2.

2026) EU law, notably Council Regulation (EU) 2025/1208 on strengthening the security of identity cards of EU citizens and of residence documents issued to EU citizens and their family members exercising their right of free movement, does not oblige Member States to include, on identity cards issued to their own nationals or residence documents issued to nationals of other Member States resident in their territory, the place of birth of the holder.
Moreover, there is no European computerised system/digital platform used for issuing identity cards; each Member State is responsible for issuing its own identity cards.

Accordingly, in the case raised by the Honourable Member, it is for the Greek authorities to decide how to describe, on identity documents and residence permits, locations in the areas of the Republic of Cyprus not under the effective control of the Government of the Republic of Cyprus.
